# Home
URL: https://www.pointercreek.com/

Welcome

Welcome to Pointer Creek Wealth Management®, an independent, owner-led, planning-first fiduciary firm serving high- and ultra-high-net-worth individuals, families, business owners, trusts, and other entities. We selectively offer fiduciary planning projects, ongoing fiduciary planning, and ongoing fiduciary wealth management, helping clients coordinate investments, retirement, taxes, estate considerations, risk management, and long-term financial objectives.

Why Pointer Creek?

Pointer Creek Wealth Management® was built around a simple idea: good financial advice should begin with understanding the client—not with selling a product, gathering an account, or fitting someone into a predetermined solution.

We are an independent, owner-led fiduciary planning and wealth management firm with deep experience serving individuals, families, business owners, trusts, and other entities with financial and planning needs that often extend well beyond an investment portfolio. We bring planning, investments, taxes, estate considerations, risk management, and long-term family objectives into one coordinated conversation.

Our job is not simply to tell clients what they want to hear. It is to ask the questions they may not know to ask, explain the tradeoffs in plain English, and provide thoughtful guidance grounded in evidence, experience, and their best interests—even when the right answer is not the easiest one.

That is what we mean when we say: see the unseen.

Fiduciary, Always

We are your fiduciary. Your interests come first. Every recommendation begins with what we believe is appropriate for you—not what benefits a product provider or our firm.

# About Pointer Creek
URL: https://www.pointercreek.com/about.html

About Pointer Creek

Pointer Creek Wealth Management® is an independent, owner-led fiduciary planning and wealth management firm in Canfield, Ohio, serving individuals, families, business owners, trusts and other entities with financial lives that often extend well beyond an investment portfolio.

We built Pointer Creek around a planning-first idea: understand the person, family or organization first; understand what the money needs to accomplish second; and only then determine what strategies, investments or other tools may be appropriate.

Our Story

Built to Practice Financial Advice Differently

Pointer Creek grew from a simple frustration with the traditional financial-services model: too often, the product or transaction comes first and the planning is expected to follow.

We wanted to build the firm in the opposite direction. That meant creating an independent, owner-led practice where planning could come first; where a client could pay us simply for advice without being required to move an investment account; where investment management could be built around the purpose of the money rather than the need to gather assets; and where saying “no,” “not yet,” or “you don’t need that” could be perfectly acceptable answers.

Over time, that approach naturally led us deeper into the financial lives of the people we serve. Retirement decisions interact with taxes. Taxes interact with investments. Investments interact with estate planning. Businesses affect families. Trusts affect beneficiaries. And decisions that look perfectly reasonable in isolation can create consequences somewhere else.

Pointer Creek exists to help connect those pieces.

We have intentionally remained a specialized firm. Our goal is never to become the largest bulk-advice or small-account asset-gathering firm we can build. It is to build an enduring one that does excellent work, treats people well, continually improves its craft, and has the capacity to give each relationship the attention it deserves.

See the unseen.

“See the unseen” is more than a tagline. It describes how we believe good planning should work.

The most consequential part of a financial decision is not always the part that is easiest to see. A reasonable investment decision can create an unnecessary tax consequence. An estate plan can be beautifully drafted but never properly funded. A retirement-income decision can affect Medicare premiums, taxes and what ultimately passes to the next generation. A strategy that solves today’s problem can quietly create another one years from now.

Our job is to look across those intersections—to ask the questions that may not be obvious, identify tradeoffs and unintended consequences, and help clients understand not only what they can do, but what a decision may mean years or even generations later.

That’s what we mean by see the unseen.

What We Believe

Planning comes before transactions — We first understand what the money is supposed to accomplish, then determine which strategies or tools may be appropriate.

Fiduciary advice requires candor — Sometimes the right answer is “no,” “not yet,” or “you don’t need that.” We’d rather give an uncomfortable answer than manufacture a comfortable one.

Complexity should be handled, not transferred — The work behind the scenes may be complicated. Our job is to make the conclusions, choices and tradeoffs understandable.

Long-term decisions matter more than short-term activity — We think in years, decades and generations, not headlines and quarters.

Small is intentional — We would rather maintain the capacity to know our clients and do excellent work than pursue growth simply for growth’s sake.

# Who We Serve
URL: https://www.pointercreek.com/who-we-serve.html

Who We Serve Best

Pointer Creek is not designed to be everything to everyone. As your fiduciary, we work best with clients who value honesty, thoughtful planning, and a long-term partnership — not shortcuts, hype, or performance theater. Our best relationships share a handful of traits that have far more to do with mindset than with age or profession.

See If We’re a Fit

The Mindsets We Work Best With

You’re interviewing us as much as we’re interviewing you — fit matters, a lot. A fiduciary partnership with us fits best when:

- You want the truth — even when it isn’t what you were hoping to hear. As your fiduciary, we won’t inflate assumptions or sugarcoat reality just to make a plan look better. You’d rather hear an honest “no” or “not yet” than a comfortable answer that won’t hold up.

- You choose to delegate as a lifestyle decision. You may be perfectly capable of managing much of this yourself. You’d simply rather entrust the details to a capable fiduciary and spend your time and energy on your family, work, passions, travel, hobbies—or whatever matters more to you.

- You want clarity, not jargon. No “strategy of the month.” You want the complexity handled behind the scenes and the conclusions and tradeoffs explained in plain English.

- You’re looking for an advisory relationship you don’t have to replace. Maybe you’ve experienced advisor fatigue, product pitching, frequent turnover, or advice that seemed to begin with someone else’s agenda. You want a long-term fiduciary relationship built around your interests instead.

- You think in decades, not quarters. You value patience, discipline, and follow-through — a long-term fiduciary thinking partner who keeps the people who come after you in mind.

If your goal requires aligning the sun, moon, stars, and a Powerball ticket, we’ll tell you—with a smile—and then build a plan around what can actually work.

Clients & Change Situations We Serve Especially Well

Pointer Creek serves the ongoing financial and planning needs of a diverse range of individuals, families, trusts, and other entities. These include privately held businesses, family limited partnerships (FLPs), private foundations, nonprofits and 501(c)(3) organizations, retirement plans, and endowments.

We also have particular depth in several change situations where thoughtful, multidisciplinary planning becomes especially valuable. These aren’t necessarily different “client types.” They’re inflection points when financial decisions begin interacting with taxes, investments, estate planning, business interests, family considerations, and long-term objectives.

‹

Newly Formed Entities & Startup Architecture

Entity choice, tax setup, and retirement structure — set right on day one.

Read more →

We help founders and new business owners make early decisions that will influence their financial and tax lives for decades. This includes:

- evaluating entity types (LLC, S-corp, C-corp, partnership, etc.),

- understanding tax classifications and long-term implications,

- assembling the right professional team (legal, tax, accounting, payroll, benefits),

- establishing retirement plans that use tax-deferred or tax-free dollars,

- designing early-stage compensation and ownership structures,

- implementing tax-managed strategies from day one.

Wise decisions on day one can save extraordinary amounts of money, time, and stress later. We help founders start strong.

Explore our fiduciary financial planning →

Entity Changes & Structural Transitions

LLC → S-corp, restructuring, trusts, and holding companies — made clear.

Read more →

We build our systems to excel at guiding entities and families through complex structural transitions, such as:

- LLC → S-corp conversions,

- S-corp ↔ C-corp transitions,

- partnership restructuring,

- evaluating ESBT vs. QSST trust qualification,

- shifting from revocable to irrevocable structures,

- assessing FLP, LLC, or holding company structures for asset protection, taxation, and succession.

These decisions often involve layers of tax, liability, and long-term planning implications. Pointer Creek translates complex permutations into clear, confident decision-making.

Business Owners Approaching Transition

Sale, succession, or exit. Like sending a child off to college — we help.

Read more →

One of our greatest areas of strength is working with business owners preparing for valuation, succession, or transition to the next phase of life. For many owners, their business has been intertwined with their identity for decades. Personal and professional finances often sit in one tightly woven knot — emotionally, legally, operationally, and financially.

We help owners unravel that knot with care, clarity, and decades of experience. Whether the transition involves:

- partial retirement,

- employee takeover or an internal successor,

- an outright sale or merger,

- liquidation,

- a phased step-back, or

- a complete and permanent exit,

we provide the financial, tax, legal-structure awareness, emotional grounding, and lifestyle planning needed to make the decision one they will not regret.

Letting go of a business can feel like sending a child off to college. We help owners navigate every part of that process — the logic, the math, and the meaning.

Explore trust & estate planning →

The Retirement Red Zone

“What got you here won’t get you there.” When saving becomes spending.

Read more →

We work extremely well with individuals and couples approaching an impending retirement date — the retirement red zone. This season often drives people to seek a new advisor because, as we tell clients:

“What got you here, won’t get you there.”

We say this because saving for retirement is very different from spending in retirement. A portfolio built for growth or self-directed accumulation may not be structured to deliver protected, tax-efficient, dependable income for decades.

We help clients transition from accumulation to distribution by analyzing:

- asset allocation and asset location,

- risk capacity vs. risk tolerance,

- sequence-of-return risk,

- Social Security interactions,

- pension timing and optimization,

- tax brackets and withdrawal strategies,

- healthcare and long-term care planning,

- the emotional and lifestyle adjustments that come with retirement.

We help clients enter retirement not just confident — but fully prepared.

Explore fiduciary wealth management →

Multiple pensions, Social Security, Railroad Retirement, employer benefits, deferred compensation, or other overlapping systems—untangled.

Read more →

We routinely guide clients through the “more-than-one” world. Think of multiple pensions, multiple retirement systems, and overlapping rules that collide in unexpected ways. Examples include:

- Social Security combined with (STRS) or State Teacher Pension

- Railroad Retirement paired with other systems

- Spouses with entirely different benefit structures, vesting schedules, and retirement timelines.

These situations demand precision, context, and clarity — which we provide through vast planning experience.

Premarital Planning, New Couples & Blended Families

Shared values, separate assets, trusts and titling — future friction reduced.

Read more →

We work closely with couples at the beginning of their financial journey together, whether a first marriage, a blended family, or late-in-life partnership. We help them plan to:

- build shared financial values

- identify hidden conflicts early

- align expectations around lifestyle and long-term goals

- coordinate separate assets responsibly

- prepare for future family considerations (children or no children)

- support entrepreneurship, relocation, or career changes

- manage multi-state property ownership

- structure trusts, LLCs, and titling to avoid probate

Our process is designed to establish long-term stability and reduce future friction. If you elect ongoing fiduciary planning after your initial plan package, we can support not only the initial level-setting and benchmarking, but ongoing support of keeping the household coordinated across combined goals, combined benefits and combined professionals.

Cabins, lake houses, hunting land, and ranches — preserved for future generations.

- create governance frameworks

A legacy property can be a blessing or a battleground — we help ensure it holds families together as intended.

Not every client comes to us during a transition — and that’s perfectly fine. Many clients seek our planning services simply because the decide it’s finally time to get organized — the classic “financial junk drawer” moment:

“I’m capable, but I’m busy… and it’s time to get my financial life cleaned up, organized, and under control.”

Clients don’t always need to be selling a business, approaching retirement, blending families, or handling multiple pensions to thrive within Pointer Creek’s ecosystem. If you’d like to flip the script, from various transactions, assets and accounts accumulated throughout life controlling and puzzling you, to you and your evidence-based plan controlling the transactions required to support it, we can help.

Where We’re Not a Fit

Honesty runs both ways. Fiduciary respect means being just as clear about who we can’t serve well:

Where we’re not a fit

- You’re looking for hot stock tips, market predictions, or something exciting to talk about on the golf course. That’s not how we manage serious money.

- You want an advisor to tell you what you want to hear. Sometimes good fiduciary advice means saying that a goal, assumption, or strategy simply doesn’t work.

- You need daily lifestyle policing or spending guardrails. If you need someone to stop the bottle service or put a hold on chartering the G650 to the beach, there are firms built for that. We’re not one of them.

- Mutual respect isn’t negotiable here. A large portfolio doesn’t excuse treating our team—or the people around you—poorly. Fit matters more than account size.

# Our Process — How We Actually Work
URL: https://www.pointercreek.com/how-we-work.html

How we actually work.

Most advisory firms describe what they sell. Very few explain how they actually work. At Pointer Creek, process matters — not because we love complexity, but because thoughtful planning, accountability, and follow-through are what protect clients from mistakes, missed steps, and conflicts of interest. Here is exactly how our real process works, from the first conversation to long-term partnership.

How New Relationships Begin

We don’t buy leads, we don’t run ads, and we don’t sponsor billboards or golf outings. In fact, we maintain a waiting list of people who would like to become clients, only onboarding when capacity and fitment align. This is only possible now, after decades of never compromising our core beliefs or putting our interests ahead those of clients. That said, not everyone finds us through an existing client referral.

Some discover Pointer Creek through careful online research, often after searching specifically for a fiduciary, a CFP® practitioner, or conflict-free advice. When they arrive at our virtual doorstep, they frequently say things like:

- “I can’t believe you actually publish your fees.”

- “I can’t believe you’re willing to work on a non-AUM model.”

- “I can’t believe you’ll just charge me for the planning, with no asset requirement.”

- “I can’t believe you built me a plan, and the answer wasn’t change everything over.”

We take those comments as signs that, for many clients, it has become unusually difficult to find a fiduciary advisor who will provide unbiased, non-proprietary advice without an automatic expectation of transferring assets or purchasing firm-specific products.

Whether you were referred by a long-time happy client or discovered us after thorough vetting and research, everyone enters the same way, with an introductory meeting.

The Introductory Meeting: Mutual Fit, Not a Sales Pitch

Every potential relationship begins with an introductory meeting. This is not a sales presentation; it’s a mutual interview. We use this to understand:

- who you are and what matters most to you

- what you’re hoping we can help with

- what success would look like six months, six years, or even decades from now

- how you prefer to make decisions

- what kind of relationship you’re looking to build with an advisory firm.

You’re evaluating us — our philosophy, our communication style, and whether you feel comfortable trusting us with your information, your goals, and your family. We’ll provide very candid information about who we are and who we are not.

By the end of this introductory meeting, we commit to giving you:

- A sense of mutual fit — whether we believe we can truly add value and whether we have capacity to serve you at the level you deserve.

- An estimate of the time, cost, and complexity involved in moving forward, if we both decide to engage.

- A clear outline of next steps in the planning process, should we determine to proceed

Planning First: A Thorough Financial Planning Process

Some clients have an immediate wealth management or risk management need and come to us wanting a single scenario or need solved, ASAP. If you know you have limited time to process your tax-free rollover and only require fiduciary investment management of your impending rollover, we’ve got you.

If you know your business needs a complex multigenerational entity-purchase funded buy-sell agreement that avoids compounding federal estate tax problems, we’ve got you. In either scenario we’re still leading with the appropriate level of planning. This doesn’t mean we take any longer than non-planning-led firms to satisfy your immediate needs and concerns.

When you hire us for “I know what I need planning” it just means we pause long enough to ask the right questions, that need to be answered, to provide you the best possible outcome.

When you hire us for “I don’t really know what I want or need yet planning,” we lead with planning and complete the full planning process before implementing any fiduciary risk management or fiduciary investment management solutions.

At Pointer Creek, your plan drives your recommendations, not our agenda. Our financial planning process, led by a CFP® professional where appropriate, in plain English looks like this:

Discovery • Data Gathering • Analysis & Modeling • Recommendations • Implementation • Monitoring & Follow-Through

That process is mostly standard for CFP® professionals. What isn’t always standard is adding in:

- 25 + years of complex-planning experience from the lead planner,

- comfort working with clients ranging from newlywed couples to $100M+ companies

- the ability to function as a “CFO for hire” or “outsourced family office” in high-need, high-frequency situations — while still maintaining capacity and quality for every other client.

Client Capacity, Waiting Lists & Realistic Timelines

We intentionally limit the number of new planning engagements we work on at one time. When our active planning capacity is full, we maintain a waiting list rather than dilute the attention given to the families and organizations already engaged with us.

A typical planning engagement may take approximately four to eight weeks, although the timeline depends heavily on the complexity of the work and how quickly the information needed for analysis becomes available. Statements, tax returns, benefit information, estate documents, business records, insurance policies, and other information often arrive in stages.

The objective is not to finish a plan as quickly as possible. It is to do the work thoroughly, ask the questions that need to be asked, and give each engagement the attention it deserves.

Systems, documentation, and quality control

We put unusual energy into documentation and follow-through — where many advisory relationships quietly fail.

- Meeting notes run through secure, encrypted dictation and internal QC.

- They become structured tasks in our practice-management software.

- Our operations manager verifies them; the firm reviews them each morning.

- A $2.5 million family and a $40 million family receive the same checklist-driven care and attention to follow-through.

We don’t leave your financial life to chance, inbox chaos, or someone’s sticky note.

Where our process goes deeper

- Estate-plan implementation & funding. An estate plan does not accomplish much sitting unfunded in a binder. We help clients coordinate ownership, beneficiary designations, trust funding, and other implementation details so the completed planning has a better chance of operating as intended.

- Estate scenario modeling & testing. We go asset by asset—from the knickknacks to the multi-million-dollar account—and run what we sometimes call a “paper assassination”: a simulated walk-through of what would actually happen under a particular death or incapacity scenario. The objective is to uncover ownership and beneficiary gaps, unnecessary probate exposure, tax considerations, administrative delays, and other problems while there is still time to address them.

- Deep-dive risk management analysis. With no allegiance to selling insurance, our planning models evaluate both risk retention (no insurance contracts) and risk transfer (including estate- or trust-owned insurance where appropriate), using multiple carriers, structures, and scenarios—comparisons that could “wrap around the conference room.” Our loyalty is to the client outcome, not to any company or policy-production target.

- Balancing wealth, life, and legacy. We’re not here to tell people to hoard every dollar. It’s not unusual for us to say, “You can afford to spend some of this.” The point isn’t to die with the largest spreadsheet; it’s to live a life—and leave a legacy—that reflects your values.

No AUM quotas, no growth targets, no hidden agenda

Pointer Creek is intentionally built to avoid the pressure that can come from quotas, production goals, outside ownership, or debt-driven growth expectations. We do not believe clients should become the raw material needed to satisfy a firm’s growth target.

Our philosophy is closer to Field of Dreams: build something worth showing up for. We focus first on doing excellent work, taking care of the people who have already trusted us, and continually improving the firm. If that earns introductions and attracts other families who value the same approach, growth can follow naturally.

Our incentives are aligned with getting the planning right—not with gathering as many assets or producing as many transactions as possible.

Does this sound like the kind of relationship you’re looking for?

An introductory meeting is a mutual conversation about what you’re trying to accomplish, whether Pointer Creek can help, and what the next step might look like. No pitch. No product. No obligation.

# Fiduciary Services
URL: https://www.pointercreek.com/services.html

Fiduciary Services

Pointer Creek Wealth Management offers a wide array of specialized fiduciary services to high- and ultra-high-net-worth families, individuals, trusts, retirement plans, charitable foundations, nonprofit organizations and other entities.

Regardless of how simple or nuanced the engagement, our services generally fall within three categories:

Fiduciary Planning Projects

What should we do?

Learn more →

Ongoing Fiduciary Planning

How does the necessary planning continue?

Learn more →

Ongoing Fiduciary Wealth Management

Who will manage the portfolio according to the plan?

Learn more →

At Pointer Creek Wealth Management®, the plan comes before the transaction.

Every relationship begins with understanding what the money is intended to accomplish. Only then do we determine what planning, investment management, implementation, or ongoing oversight may be appropriate.

The amount of planning required depends upon the decision being made. For one client, that may mean a narrowly defined planning project addressing a single retirement account. For another, it may mean a comprehensive financial, retirement, tax and estate-planning engagement involving multiple generations, businesses, trust structures, properties and outside professionals.

Planning establishes where you’re going. From there, you decide which responsibilities you want to retain—and which you want Pointer Creek to assume in helping you get there.

A Simple Way to Think About It

“What should we do?”

Start with a Fiduciary Planning Project. Pointer Creek analyzes the situation, develops the architecture and provides the roadmap.

“How does the planning continue?”

Choose Ongoing Fiduciary Planning. Pointer Creek proactively monitors, coordinates & advances the planning process.

“Who will manage the portfolio according to the plan?”

Choose Ongoing Fiduciary Wealth Management. Pointer Creek assumes ongoing fiduciary responsibility for assets accepted under our management.

Combining Our Services

Clients may use one, two, or all three service models depending on their needs and the responsibilities they want to delegate. Some clients engage Pointer Creek for a planning project and implement the recommendations themselves. Others ask us to continue the planning, manage investment assets according to the plan, or assume both responsibilities.

None of these arrangements is inherently better than another. The appropriate relationship depends on what you want to accomplish, what you prefer to handle yourself, and what you would rather delegate to us.

The appropriate relationship depends upon what responsibilities you want to retain and what responsibilities you want to delegate.

When clients ask Pointer Creek to assume more than one of these responsibilities, an obvious question follows: how should the combined relationship be priced?

Integrated Relationship Pricing

Because each service is priced on a stand-alone basis, some responsibilities become more efficient when performed together. When Pointer Creek provides both Ongoing Fiduciary Planning and Ongoing Fiduciary Wealth Management, activities that might otherwise require outside statements, telephone calls, transfer instructions, third-party coordination and separate implementation can often be incorporated into the ongoing relationship.

So a separate planning fee can appropriately coexist with a reduced asset-management rate — transparent pricing for the responsibilities Pointer Creek is actually being asked to assume.

How Our Services Are Priced

Pointer Creek intentionally separates the pricing of fiduciary planning projects, ongoing fiduciary planning, and ongoing fiduciary wealth management because each service solves a different problem and places different responsibilities with our firm.

- Fiduciary Planning Projects — priced according to the scope and complexity of the planning work. These may range from a narrowly defined question to a comprehensive financial, retirement, tax, estate, or family planning architecture.

- Ongoing Fiduciary Planning — generally structured with an initial design-and-architecture fee followed by an ongoing advisory retainer. Pricing reflects the complexity of the planning and the ongoing responsibilities Pointer Creek agrees to assume.

- Ongoing Fiduciary Wealth Management — generally priced as an asset-management fee for portfolios accepted under our discretionary management. The fee reflects our ongoing responsibility for portfolio construction, investment selection, monitoring, trading, rebalancing, and implementation.

Not sure which service model fits your situation?

You don’t need to decide before contacting us. An introductory conversation can help clarify what you’re trying to accomplish, what responsibilities you want to retain, and where Pointer Creek may be able to help.

# Fiduciary Planning Projects
URL: https://www.pointercreek.com/service-planning-projects.html

“What should we do?”

Fiduciary Planning Projects

Project planning answers a defined planning question or builds a defined planning architecture.

Every Pointer Creek relationship begins with planning, but that does not mean every client requires a comprehensive financial plan.

A Fiduciary Planning Project may be narrowly focused on a single decision or may encompass virtually every aspect of a family’s financial life. The scope and fee are established based upon the planning work actually required.

Examples may include:

- Retirement and financial independence planning

- Retirement-income and distribution planning

- Estate and legacy planning

- Investment and portfolio analysis

- Retirement-plan or rollover analysis

- Social Security and pension decisions

- Tax-aware planning and Roth conversion analysis

- Business-owner and succession planning

- Risk-management and insurance analysis

- Charitable planning

- Trust and beneficiary planning

- Family Limited Partnership analysis

- Advanced estate-tax planning and strategy modeling

- Premarital or family financial planning

- A comprehensive financial, tax, retirement and estate-planning architecture

A planning project has a defined beginning, defined scope and defined conclusion. Pointer Creek analyzes the agreed-upon matters, develops recommendations and provides an implementation roadmap.

When the engagement concludes, responsibility for implementation, ongoing monitoring and recognizing when circumstances warrant another planning review generally returns to you.

For many organized, financially sophisticated clients who enjoy this type of work, this is exactly the “DIY with professional guidance” relationship they want.

When Project-Based Planning May Be a Good Fit

- You have a specific planning question or event to address.

- You want comprehensive recommendations but are comfortable implementing them yourself.

- You already have staff or systems responsible for ongoing implementation and monitoring.

- Your circumstances are relatively stable and you prefer to return for planning assistance when you determine it is needed.

- You want an independent fiduciary analysis without necessarily establishing an ongoing advisory relationship.

- Your need is truly a one-time event, outside the scope of your expertise.

Clients who disengage at the conclusion of a planning project are welcome to return for additional services when needed. Future updates, implementation assistance and new planning projects are available at then-current pricing.

Explore Related Planning Topics: Retirement Planning · Estate & Legacy Planning · Tax-Aware Planning · Risk Management · Investment & Portfolio Analysis

# Ongoing Fiduciary Planning
URL: https://www.pointercreek.com/service-ongoing-planning.html

“How does the necessary planning continue?”

Ongoing Fiduciary Planning

Ongoing Fiduciary Planning means Pointer Creek takes responsibility for keeping the planning process active.

When your initial planning project is completed, you have an architecture from which to work. The next question is who will be responsible for keeping it current?

Who owns responsibility for keeping the planning process alive?

Project-based planning, that responsibility generally returns to you.

Ongoing Fiduciary Planning, you delegate the bulk of that responsibility to Pointer Creek.

Rather than waiting for you to recognize the next planning need, Pointer Creek proactively reviews applicable planning issues, identifies planning triggers, advances agreed-upon priorities, coordinates implementation and revisits strategies as circumstances change.

Ongoing Fiduciary Planning can take different forms depending on the complexity of the relationship and the responsibilities delegated to Pointer Creek. For some clients, that may mean recurring retirement, tax, estate, benefit, or family-planning coordination. More complex relationships may involve closely held businesses, trusts, multiple entities, significant real estate, charitable interests, multigenerational planning, and coordination among attorneys, CPAs and other professional advisors.

We refer to this deeper level of ongoing coordination as Family & Private Enterprise Advisory Services. All Family & Private Enterprise Advisory relationships include ongoing fiduciary planning, but not every Ongoing Fiduciary Planning relationship requires that level of coordination.

For a very limited number of families, the scope of an ongoing relationship may extend further into what is commonly described as a fractional family office relationship. These engagements involve a substantially greater degree of coordination, administration and delegated responsibility and are accepted selectively based on the family’s needs and Pointer Creek’s capacity to provide the appropriate level of service.

What Ongoing Planning May Include

- Recurring financial and family planning reviews

- Annual tax and retirement-distribution planning

- Ongoing Roth conversion and tax-bracket analysis

- Regular Estate taxation, liquidity and beneficiary intent monitoring

- Liquidity and spending coordination for major items that impact retirement or estate planning

- Implementation tracking and scheduled follow-through

- Coordination with attorneys, CPAs and other professionals

- Family and generational planning as it appears or changes

- Monitoring significant legislative and tax changes, modeling their impact to your plan goals and/or opportunities or challenges they may create

- Event-driven planning when circumstances change

- Basic planning, critical documents, and education for dependent family members where appropriate

- Customized benefit election and coordination with changes to employment or employer benefit packages

Unlike a project engagement, there is no predetermined point at which Pointer Creek simply hands the planning responsibility back to you. Our responsibility to monitor, coordinate and adapt the agreed-upon planning strategies continues, on a defined planning calendar with multiple scheduled milestones throughout the year, for as long as you retain the service.

When Ongoing Fiduciary Planning May Be a Good Fit

- You want someone other than yourself responsible for remembering what needs to happen next.

- Your planning includes strategies that should be evaluated annually or throughout the year.

- Your tax, estate, retirement, family or business decisions frequently interact.

- You want Pointer Creek coordinating with your CPA, attorney and other professionals towards your specific plan goals.

- Your family circumstances or financial structure change frequently enough that a five-year planning event is unlikely to be sufficient.

- You value proactive planning rather than returning only when you recognize a new issue yourself.

Ongoing Fiduciary Planning is generally priced using an initial design and architecture fee followed by a recurring advisory retainer. Pricing is based primarily upon planning complexity and the ongoing responsibilities accepted by Pointer Creek rather than net worth alone. Generally speaking, the initial design and architecture fee will be lower than a comparable one-time planning project, to offset the anticipated ongoing planning retainer.

Explore Related Planning Topics: Family & Private Enterprise Advisory · Estate & Legacy Planning · Retirement & Tax Planning · Risk Management

# Ongoing Fiduciary Wealth Management
URL: https://www.pointercreek.com/service-ongoing-wealth.html

“Who will manage the portfolio according to the plan?”

Ongoing Fiduciary Wealth Management

Fiduciary Wealth Management takes responsibility for managing the portfolio.

Planning establishes what an investment account is intended to accomplish. Ongoing Fiduciary Wealth Management puts that investment strategy into practice.

Before accepting assets for ongoing management, Pointer Creek first seeks to understand the purpose of the assets, expected time horizon, anticipated distributions, tax considerations, risk tolerance and capacity, and how the account fits within the client’s broader financial circumstances.

The amount of planning necessary may be very limited for a straightforward account or substantially more extensive for a complex household, trust(s), retirement plan(s) or institutional relationship.

When Pointer Creek accepts an investment-management engagement, we assume ongoing fiduciary responsibility for the assets entrusted to our management, which may include:

- Portfolio construction and asset allocation

- Investment selection and implementation

- Ongoing monitoring of investments within the account

- Trading and regular (quarterly) rebalancing of the account

- Establishing risk management controls and monitoring

- Cash and liquidity management

- Portfolio-related distributions

- Tax-aware investment management where applicable

- Coordination among managed account types

- Investment-policy development and monitoring

Ongoing Fiduciary Wealth Management is for the portfolio. It does not, by itself, mean Pointer Creek has accepted responsibility for continuously monitoring every aspect of the client’s financial, tax, estate, business or family planning. That broader responsibility belongs within an Ongoing Fiduciary Planning engagement discussed in the previous section.

When Ongoing Fiduciary Wealth Management May Be a Good Fit

- You want to delegate day-to-day portfolio-management, trading, rebalancing, investment selection and monitoring responsibility.

- You want your investments implemented according to a defined planning purpose and investment strategy.

- You prefer ongoing professional monitoring, rebalancing and implementation rather than managing the portfolio yourself.

- Your assets and circumstances are appropriate for Pointer Creek’s investment-management platform and relationship requirements.

Not every planning client will be an appropriate fit for ongoing investment management. Pointer Creek evaluates investment-management engagements based upon the assets involved, required services, operational considerations and the economics necessary to responsibly maintain the relationship.

When ongoing investment management is not appropriate, Pointer Creek may still provide planning, investment analysis, allocation guidance and other project-based advice for assets the client manages directly or holds elsewhere.

Already Have an Established Portfolio?

Transferring an investment account to Pointer Creek does not automatically mean selling everything already in it. Before trading, we review the investments that arrive, the intended portfolio strategy and, for taxable accounts, the available tax-lot information.

Existing holdings may be retained, transitioned over time, or replaced depending on their investment merits, tax consequences, portfolio role and the client’s broader planning objectives. Our models provide an investment framework, but they are not intended to force unnecessary transactions merely for the sake of immediate uniformity.

Every transition begins with the same question: What is in this client’s best interest?

Learn more about how we transition existing portfolios →

Not sure which responsibilities you want to retain and which you want to delegate?

You don’t need to decide before contacting us. That’s one of the things an introductory conversation can help clarify.

# Fees & Transparency
URL: https://www.pointercreek.com/fees-transparency.html

Fees & Transparency

Transparency should not be rare.

We publish our fees for a simple reason: fairness and consistency. Here’s how we get paid, why we don’t require assets to work with you, and why our incentives are built to align with yours.

See Published Pricing & Documents

How we get paid

Pointer Creek is compensated in two primary ways: fiduciary asset management and financial planning. We intentionally offer both, because different clients—and different situations—require different approaches.

- Fiduciary asset management — turnkey and fully discretionary: investment selection, trading, rebalancing, monitoring, and distributions handled for you.

- Financial planning — structured flat-fee project packages, or a-la-carte/hourly planning for a specific question, so you never face open-ended billing anxiety.

Why we publish our fees

Each year we benchmark planning and wealth-management firms in our region — often with local finance interns. The result is consistent: more than 90% of responses come down to “it depends.”

So we do it differently

- You know what to expect before engaging.

- No advantage to being a more assertive negotiator.

- No client subsidizes another’s discount.

- No one is overcharged because pricing wasn’t clear.

We know our services and the effort to deliver them well — and we’re comfortable standing behind that pricing publicly.

Why we’re not a pure AUM firm

Assets alone don’t tell the whole story — and charging by them isn’t always fair.

Often underserved by AUM-only firms

- A surgeon completing residency.

- An entrepreneur building a business.

- A family expecting a future inheritance.

- Anyone facing a complex tax or estate decision without a large balance yet.

Some of our most valuable long-term relationships began before assets accumulated. Our structure lets us serve both — fairly.

Why planning first matters

All good results come from planning. There’s no responsible way to invest without first understanding when the money is needed, how it’ll be used, what risks are acceptable, and what you’re trying to achieve. Without it, clients get cookie-cutter recommendations — the same allocation, the same products, regardless of situation.

Thoughtful planning leads to better decisions, better decisions to better outcomes, and better outcomes to long-term trust.

Our goal isn’t to gather assets quickly; it’s to understand clients deeply and build recommendations that hold up over time.

Fiduciary alignment & long-term incentives

Our incentives are structured to align with clients — not short-term production goals.

- No quarterly asset-gathering targets or production quotas.

- No directives from outside shareholders — we’re independent and owner-led.

- No intention of becoming a publicly traded company.

That lets us decide with a long-term perspective — measured in decades, not quarters. The question is always what’s best for the client’s life, family, and long-term outcome, not what looks best on a quarterly report.

Our billing philosophy: built for fairness

Our billing structure exists for one reason: fairness. Across thousands of advisor interactions before founding Pointer Creek, one thing was clear — most firms struggle to apply pricing consistently. So we built one where pricing is clearly defined, service is consistently delivered, and you know exactly what you’re paying for.

When clients couldn’t fully use a service they’d engaged — due to time or life circumstances — we’ve proactively reduced fees, on our own initiative. Repeatedly.

Clients should never feel they’re overpaying, underserved, or misunderstood.

# Frequently Asked Questions
URL: https://www.pointercreek.com/faq.html

Plain answers.

What is the minimum to work with Pointer Creek?
For a managed account, $500,000+ in net investible assets. Planning is scoped to complexity rather than a minimum — so if you’re not there yet, our planning-only services are still open to you.

Do I need to be wealthy to work with a fiduciary?
No. Alongside wealth management, we offer planning-only, pay-for-what-you-need services — and some of our best long-term relationships began before the assets accumulated.

Do you require me to move my assets to you?
No. We publish our fees and aren’t a pure AUM firm. You can engage us for planning without moving a single dollar — and we’ll tell you honestly when moving assets isn’t in your interest.

Will you sell all my current investments when I transfer my account?
Not automatically. Your first model trade is the starting point for our analysis, not an instruction to liquidate — we protect tax lots and keep good holdings where it serves you.

Do you have a waiting list?
Often, yes. We actively work on only ten financial plans at a time, so every engagement gets real attention rather than rushed work; when one finishes, the next moves from the list to active.

How can I schedule a consultation?
Call (234) 414-1014 or email team@pointercreek.com. The first step is a short introductory meeting to see whether we’re a mutual fit.

Are you actually a fiduciary?
Yes — a CFP®-only practice, so there’s nobody here to hand you off to. We act in your interest across the whole relationship, not only on the products we sell.

How do you protect my financial information?
Secure, encrypted storage and transmission, background-checked staff, and internal controls on who can access what. We treat your data the way we’d want ours treated.

Do you sell proprietary products?
No — and no product quotas, either. We have no in-house funds to push and no incentive to steer you toward one strategy over another.

How long does planning actually take?
Weeks to months, depending on complexity and how quickly you return your “homework.” A typical plan runs about four to eight weeks — an honest estimate rather than an attractive one.

Will you beat the market?
We won’t promise to, and we’d be skeptical of anyone who guarantees it. Some years a portfolio beats its benchmark and some years it won’t — what matters is that your plan still reaches your goals either way. We aim to capture what the markets offer without taking risks you can’t afford, rather than chasing headlines.

Will you tell me if I don’t need you?
Yes, and we do it fairly often. If a one-time project or a second opinion is all you need, we’ll say so — sending you off with an answer instead of signing you up.

Do you work with my CPA and attorney?
Directly. We coordinate with your existing tax and legal advisors so the plan is executed as one team — and we’re glad to bring in ours if you don’t have them.

Where are you, and who do you serve?
201 South Broad Street, Canfield, Ohio 44406. We serve families across Northeast Ohio, and work with clients elsewhere by video.

What happens in the first meeting?
A conversation, not a pitch. Bring the question that’s been keeping you up; we’ll give you an honest read on fit and clear next steps — even if that means pointing you elsewhere. Start one here.

Still Have Questions? Reach Out →
